note: NOT_FULL_REGISTRY_IMPLEMENTATION — two lessons from the first real run's controlled hold; the broader Autonomous Run Contract System / Loop Contract Engine / Repository Stewardship / full Failure-to-Control Registry are NOT implemented here.

lessons.lesson: Teardown success requires BOTH Git-registration absence AND filesystem absence. A null or UNKNOWN teardown state can never pass; failure preserves evidence and holds BEFORE the next job. A provider that never ran reports TEARDOWN_NOT_ATTEMPTED (a provider outcome), not a teardown defect.
lessons.closed_in: FG-LRCQ-ACT-023 (real-provider teardown_status enum; harness provider-failure-vs-teardown split)

lessons.lesson: Held, failed, defect, and unknown terminals must be exhaustively mapped; no default may convert them to clean queue exhaustion; every observer layer (recovery, supervisor, witness, terminal report, founder projection) must preserve the authoritative terminal class.
lessons.closed_in: FG-LRCQ-ACT-023 (supervisor-main exhaustive mapping; health-witness held-terminal -> HELD)

lessons.lesson: A missing process.json must not be read as 'not invoked'. The provider lifecycle (NOT_ATTEMPTED / SPAWN_ATTEMPTED / SPAWNED / OUTPUT_RECEIVED / COST_RECORDED / COMPLETED / FAILED / UNKNOWN) must be durably distinguishable. In the first real run the truth (PROVIDER_NOT_ATTEMPTED) was recoverable only by cross-reading transactions + absent evidence; a durable per-stage record is now emitted.
